title: Flat submodule in a universally exact sequence
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ be a universally exact short exact sequence of $R$-modules, meaning that tensoring this sequence over $R$ with every $R$-module remains exact. If $M_2$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then $M_1$ is flat over $R$.

proof.text: Let $0\to N\to N'\to N''\to0$ be any short exact sequence of $R$-modules, with $N''$ the cokernel of the injection $N\to N'$. Tensoring the universally exact sequence $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$ with each of $N$, $N'$, and $N''$ gives three short exact rows. Tensoring $0\to N\to N'\to N''\to0$ with the flat module $M_2$ gives an injective middle vertical map $M_2\otimes_RN\to M_2\otimes_RN'$. Thus these maps form a commutative 3\times3 diagram with exact rows and an injective middle vertical arrow.

proof.text: For an injection $N\to N'$ and $x\in M_1\otimes_RN$ mapping to zero in $M_1\otimes_RN'$, commutativity of the left square makes the image of $x$ in $M_2\otimes_RN$ map to zero in $M_2\otimes_RN'$. The middle vertical map is injective by Step 1, so that image in $M_2\otimes_RN$ is zero. Exactness of the top row then gives $x=0$. Hence $M_1\otimes_RN\to M_1\otimes_RN'$ is injective for every injection $N\to N'$, and $M_1$ is flat by the definition of flatness.
